name: content-visibility CSS property - CSS | MDN - MDN Web Docs
snippet: The content-visibility CSS property controls whether or not an element renders its contents at all, along with forcing a strong set of containments, allowing user agents to potentially omit large swathes of layout and rendering work until it becomes needed.

name: content-visibility: the new CSS property that boosts your
snippet: The CSS content-visibility property enables web content rendering performance benefits by skipping rendering of off-screen content. This article shows you how to use this new CSS property for faster initial load times, using the auto keyword.

name: CSS Containment & Content-Visibility: Rescuing the Main
snippet: Rendering massive DOMs destroys your Interaction to Next Paint (INP) score. Here is a deep dive into how to use the contain property and content-visibility: auto to isolate layout and paint calculations, saving precious main thread computation time.

name: Optimizing Web Rendering with CSS Content-Visibility
snippet: A technical deep-dive into the CSS content-visibility property. Learn how to optimize browser rendering tree calculations and improve Largest Contentful Paint.

name: How CSS content-visibility Works and How It Can Improve
snippet: As the web.dev guide explains, content-visibility: auto applies layout, style, and paint containment. When the contents aren't relevant to the user, the browser can skip more of the work for that subtree.

name: content-visibility: auto for Long Animated Lists — css
snippet: Skip layout and paint for off-screen rows, size the placeholders honestly with contain-intrinsic-size, and keep entry animations working when rows come into view.
